title: Inkling 2 Small: training in 4-bit
kicker: What was disclosed, what it cost, and a plan
blurb: A look at how Inkling 2 Small was trained in native 4-bit, what the run probably cost, and how a smaller team could climb to the same recipe.
description: Thinking Machines released Inkling 2 Small on November 5, a 594 billion parameter mixture of experts model trained natively in 4-bit. The film pieces together what was disclosed, estimates compute and cost, and turns it into a staged plan for 4-bit pre-training and post-training. Facts, estimates and guesses are labeled.
takeaways: The first pre-training phase, 8.4 trillion tokens, took 68 hours on GB300 racks, running in NVFP4 (a 4-bit format with block scales).
Public NVFP4 recipes keep sensitive layers in higher precision and use stochastic rounding on gradients only.
The joint reinforcement learning run used 2,048 GPUs for nine days, likely more GPU hours than all of pre-training.
The lab's own cost is not disclosed, so the film's roughly 10 to 60 million dollar total is an estimate, not a reported figure.
A team should climb a ladder of small 4-bit experiments with clear gates before attempting a large run.
